task_description: Write a method in Dafny to set all even bits of a given number.
specification_response:
method SetAllEvenBits(n: int) returns (result: int)
Postconditions_prompt:
- The result has all even-positioned bits (0-based indexing) set to 1
- The bits at odd positions in the result are unchanged from the input number n
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method SetEvenBits(n: int) returns (result: int)

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - There are no preconditions; the method works for any integer input.

Dafny specification:
    // No preconditions needed
    // (The method should handle any integer input)

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The output number has all its even bits set to 1, regardless of the input bits
- The odd bits of the input number remain unchanged

Dafny specification:
    ensures (result & 0x55555555) == (n & 0x55555555) // odd bits unchanged
    ensures (result | 0x55555555) == result // all even bits are set to 1

Note: 0x55555555 is a mask with bits set at all even positions (assuming 32-bit integer).

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method SetEvenBits(n: int) returns (result: int)
    ensures (result & 0x55555555) == (n & 0x55555555) // odd bits unchanged
    ensures (result | 0x55555555) == result // all even bits are set to 1
{
    // Set all even bits to 1 by OR-ing with the mask
    result := n | 0x55555555;
}
```
